mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions "the difference between the number of X and Y have", interpret it as the signed subtraction X − Y, preserving the order of the variables as given. This keeps the sign information needed for later equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement that uses the phrase "difference between ..." to compare two quantities.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "the difference between A and B" as |A − B|, losing the sign and causing equations to be wrong.

mathgap.title: Directed "has more than" Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form "A has N more than B" into the equation A − B = N, preserving direction. Do not impose an extra constraint that A > B beyond the equation itself.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement that says "has N more than".
mathgap.example: Assuming "A has 5 more than B" forces A > B and discarding a solution where the equation yields a negative B.

mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Process each "A gives N Y to B" statement in the order it appears, immediately subtracting N from A and adding N to B. Later statements refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer (give) statement is present.
mathgap.example: Applying all transfers after processing other statements, ignoring the order in which they occur.

mathgap.title: Immediate Count Update on Direct Assignment
mathgap.principle: Treat each direct count statement "A has N Y" as setting A's current count at that point, overriding any previous value. Subsequent statements use this updated count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement provides an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Treating "A has 10 Y" as an immutable initial value and not updating it after earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in Difference Equations
mathgap.principle: For statements like "The number of Y that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of Y that C and D have", translate to (A − B) = (C − D), keeping the order of C and D exactly as written.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any comparison‑transfer statement that equates one difference to another.
mathgap.example: Reversing the order on the right‑hand side, interpreting (C − D) as (D − C).

mathgap.title: Interpret "increase by X times" as multiplicative increase
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "The number of Y that A has increases by N times", treat it as A ← A × (1 + N). In other words, add N times the current amount to the existing amount. This applies to integer and fractional N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement that uses the phrase "increases by ... times".
mathgap.example: Interpreting "increase by 5/3 times" as multiplying the current count by 5/3, which yields a non‑integer result, instead of multiplying by (1 + 5/3) = 8/3.

mathgap.title: Split equally among recipients
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X splits all the Y they own equally among A and B", set X's count to 0 and give each of A and B half of X's previous count, conserving the total Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement containing "splits ... equally among" with two recipients.
mathgap.example: Leaving X with half of the amount after splitting, thereby double‑counting the Y.

mathgap.title: Redistribute equally between two persons
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "A and B redistribute their Y to ensure each has an equal amount", compute total = A + B and set both A and B to total / 2 (allowing fractions if necessary). This conserves the total and equalizes the two counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement containing "redistribute ... to ensure each has an equal amount".
mathgap.example: Adding the average to each person without removing the original amounts, resulting in double the total.

mathgap.description: Interpreting "difference between X and Y" as an absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes differences are always non‑negative and drops the sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Keep the order of the variables and treat the expression as X − Y, preserving sign.

mathgap.description: Applying all transfers after processing other statements, ignoring their sequential effect.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as independent of order, like batch updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer in the order it appears, updating counts immediately.

mathgap.description: Assuming "A has N more than B" implies A > B and discarding solutions where the computed difference is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model adds an unnecessary inequality constraint based on the wording.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Use the equation A − B = N without imposing extra sign constraints.

mathgap.description: Treating a direct count statement as an immutable initial value and not updating it after earlier transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model thinks explicit counts are fixed once given.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Update the person's count at the point of the direct assignment, overriding any previous value.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting "increase by X times" as multiplying by X (or adding X) instead of multiplying by (1 + X).
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrasing is ambiguous and the model defaults to a simple multiplication or addition.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply the rule that "increase by N times" means add N times the current amount, i.e., multiply by (1 + N).
